name: Integration and origin attribution on every request
what: Requests carry origin (api, js-sdk@x, mcp..., website) and an optional integration tag from a closed list (n8n, zapier, make, pipedream, dify, flowise, langchain, llamaindex, crewai, raycast, cli, and others) used for analytics, rate decisions and keyless gating.
how: integrationSchema enum in utils/integration.ts; SDKs inject origin; keyless soft-gates on origin/integration (spoofable, backed by per-IP caps); MCP action logs and request logs record origin and integration.
verevonRelevance: Cheap to add to Quarry and Verevon: tag each Quarry call with caller surface (chat, agent, import, monitor) for Control Plane analytics and cost attribution.
notes: The closed enum means new partners require an API change.

name: Agent run exported as a reusable skill and workflow
what: GET /v2/agent/:id/skill distils a finished run into skill {name, spec, skillMd, workflow, schema}, a blueprint and generation timestamp: a SKILL.md for a coding agent plus a script that reproduces the run through the API.
how: AgentSkillResponse; the upstream shape is passed through verbatim by agentSkillController; paired with the skills catalog CI sync.
verevonRelevance: Aligns with Quarry's procedure compile/check work (baseline Known gap 13: procedures have no store or replay): turning a successful web-agent run into a stored, replayable procedure is exactly this loop.
notes: Generation logic is in the external agent service.

name: Build skills and endpoint-selection guidance shipped as product surface
what: Five 'build' skills teach coding agents how to integrate Firecrawl: choose /scrape for a known URL, /search for a query, /interact when clicks are needed, and route paper or developer questions to the specialised indexes; freshness (maxAge, cacheState) and liveness are treated separately; skills are mirrored into a public catalog by CI.
how: skills/ (firecrawl-build umbrella, onboarding, scrape, search, interact) with references (project-intake, endpoint-selection, integration-patterns, verification); sync-skills-catalog workflow; cross-skill links are sibling-relative so installed skills resolve flat.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's tool descriptions for the Model Plane could be written the same way: narrowest-endpoint-first routing rules, freshness vs liveness distinction, and a verification step.

name: Exchange publisher side: bounties, supply keys and applications
what: Third parties can publish data providers to the Exchange: create bounties for missing data sources, apply, claim and submit, register supply and ingest endpoints, view analytics and rates, manage platform capacity, and accept provider terms.
how: routes/exchange.ts mounts /exchange rewritten to /v1 on FIRE_EXCHANGE_URL with x-exchange-team-id set from the authenticated team; most routes require the team flag exchangeRetrieve; a bounty blocklist rejects bounties that target blocked domains.
verevonRelevance: A two-sided provider marketplace is out of Verevon's near-term scope, but integration-corev2's provider-action catalog could adopt the 'capability + terms + price' record shape.
notes: Exchange upstream is external; only the proxy and contracts are visible.

name: In-product support agent exposed as API
what: POST /v2/support/ask and /v2/support/docs-search forward questions to a support agent with their own tight rate limits (3/min).
how: supportProxyController forwards to SUPPORT_AGENT_URL under RateLimiterMode.SupportAsk and SupportDocsSearch.
verevonRelevance: Minor; shows docs-search as an API for agents that need to look up product usage.

name: Open-source core versus hosted cloud split
what: The AGPL-3.0 repo contains the API, workers, Playwright service and SDKs (SDKs MIT); the hosted product adds fire-engine browsers and proxies, FirePDF, the agent service, dashboard, Hangar sessions, Exchange and more, none of which are in the repo.
how: README 'Open Source vs Cloud' image and text; many controllers proxy to env-configured upstream URLs (FIRE_ENGINE_BETA_URL, FIRE_PDF_BASE_URL, HANGAR_URL, EXTRACT_V3_BETA_URL, FIRE_EXCHANGE_URL, LABS_SEARCH_URL, RESEARCH_PROXY_URL, SEARCH_PLATFORM_URL); SELF_HOST.md warns the default stack is unauthenticated and has no persistent volumes.
verevonRelevance: Everything differentiating (anti-bot engine, OCR, agent, browser fleet) is closed; Verevon's Quarry-v2 owns these capabilities itself, so parity should be measured against the hosted product's behaviour, not the OSS repo.
notes: Important caveat for any 'feature parity' claim based only on this repo.

name: Labs search data sources, packs and configs
what: A /labs proxy lets teams register search data sources (sites, documents, pages), refresh them, enable provider packs and save named search configurations.
how: routes/labs.ts forwards to LABS_SEARCH_URL with LABS_SEARCH_SECRET and a 120 s timeout: POST /labs/search, /labs/search/data/{sites,documents,pages}, refresh, /providers, /packs, /configs.
verevonRelevance: Closest Firecrawl analogue to presets and per-tenant search corpora; Quarry's presets are unmounted (baseline section 6) and tenant corpora live in the Data Plane.
notes: Experimental; upstream not visible.

name: Agent run trace: canonical, ordered event stream with artifact snapshots
what: GET /v2/agent/:id/trace returns every event of a run (events[], creditsUsed, activeBrowserSessions with liveViewUrl and viewport) and GET /v2/agent/:id/snapshots/:snapshotId returns the content of an artifact version.
how: Events share an envelope (schemaVersion, eventId, runId, occurredAt, producerSequence, agent{id, role orchestrator|subagent|system, name, parentId}) and a type: run.started, run.cancel_requested, run.finished, agent.started, agent.finished, browser.session.started/finished, progress.reported, reasoning.summary, tool_call.started/finished, artifact.updated, error.occurred; artifact descriptors give kind (json, markdown, html, screenshot, text), path, snapshotId, change (init|partial|append|modify|update), changedFields; errors are {code cancelled|credit_limit_reached|parent_finished|refused|internal, source agent|tool|billing|system, retryable}.
verevonRelevance: A strong template for Model Plane run events surfaced to the Verevon UI: sequence numbers for ordering, parent-agent identity for sub-agents, artifact versions as snapshots, retryable typed errors.
notes: usage.recorded events are internal and never exposed; reasoning is exposed only as summaries.

name: Request correlation, origin tags and job access TTLs
what: Every request logs an id, kind, api_version, origin, integration, target hint, ZDR flag and api key id; callers can pass x-request-id (also forwarded to Exchange and research upstreams and used as the paid-charge idempotency key); job results and access rows expire (crawl 24 h by default).
how: logRequest writes a request row (the job log transport is Pub/Sub only since 2026-10-09 per git #5010); externalRequestId reads x-request-id or External-Request-Id; job-access-store and operational-job-access keep per-job team ownership with expiry; ZDR requests skip tracing entirely (traces keyed by id are suppressed).
verevonRelevance: Quarry should accept and propagate an x-request-id from the gateway into events/receipts so a user-visible run can be traced across Gateway, Model Plane and Quarry, and ZDR must suppress tracing as here.

name: SIEM forwarding and per-request audit attribution
what: Enterprise teams can stream scrape activity (success, failure, blocked, cancelled, with threat decisions) to Azure Sentinel; callers may pass auditMetadata.username to attribute a request to an end user.
how: PUT /v2/team/siem with tenantId, clientId, encrypted clientSecret, dceUrl (must be an Azure Monitor ingestion endpoint), dcrImmutableId and Custom- stream name; batching worker, delivery metrics and a test endpoint; an ARM/DCR deployment template ships in apps/siem/azure-sentinel; encrypted at rest with SIEM_LOGGING_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Control Plane owns audit; Quarry should emit per-request audit events with an end-user attribution field into that stream, which is the same shape.
notes: Only Azure Sentinel is supported as a destination.

name: Self-hosting posture and operational warnings
what: A Compose stack (API, workers, Playwright, Redis, RabbitMQ, NuQ Postgres, optional FoundationDB) runs the open-source core on port 3002; the guide stresses an unauthenticated default, no persistence and no production architecture, with AI features off until a model provider is configured.
how: docker-compose.yaml sets resource limits (api 4 CPU/8 GB, Playwright 2 CPU/4 GB, no-new-privileges, cap_drop ALL, tmpfs); SELF_HOST.md lists 'before production' duties; Kubernetes and Helm examples exist; USE_DB_AUTHENTICATION=false is the first-run default.
verevonRelevance: A useful negative example: Verevon's compose stacks should keep auth, persistence and ZDR on by default and not rely on operators to add them.
notes: CORS is the Express default (all origins) at apps/api/src/index.ts line 89 and the JSON body limit is 10 MB.

name: Quality gates: e2e 'snips', knip, and an on-demand scrape-quality eval
what: Contributors are told to write end-to-end tests against a harness-started stack, gate tests by TEST_SUITE_SELF_HOSTED, never bypass the knip dead-code check, and can trigger a scrape-quality evaluation on a PR with a tag.
how: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; pnpm harness starts API and workers; vitest e2e under src/__tests__/snips; scrape-evals.yml runs on issue comment or PR text '#scrape-quality-eval' after an org-membership check; eval-prod.yml runs production evals; 373 test files.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's SCOREBOARD/benchmarks are not run (baseline Known gap 16); a PR-triggered quality eval with a fixed corpus is the cheap way to keep parity claims honest.

name: Live view and interactive takeover URLs on every session
what: Each browser or interact session returns a CDP URL for automation, a liveViewUrl (read-only stream) and an interactiveLiveViewUrl (a human can click and type in the same session); the agent trace also lists active sessions with their live view and viewport so a UI can attach to a running agent.
how: browserSessionLinks returns cdpUrl, liveViewUrl (cdp_path) and interactiveLiveViewUrl (cdp_interactive_path); streamWebView defaults to true; the README interact example returns liveViewUrl; agent trace supports liveView=true. The repo contains no UI: the dashboard and playground that render these are outside it.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's BrowserChrome already has live view, takeover, devtools, timeline and approvals; the API-level lesson is that attach/takeover are just URLs on the session object, with takeover a separate, explicitly named capability.
notes: Quarry baseline Known gap 11: takeover is advisory server-side and receipts do not type the initiator; Firecrawl's two-URL split (read-only vs interactive) is cleaner.

name: Session recording as HLS replay
what: A session created with recordSession:true can be replayed afterwards: GET /v2/browser/:id/replay returns a single page entry with start and end times and GET /v2/browser/:id/replay/0 returns an HLS playlist.
how: browserReplayController looks up the recording by context_id, sets Cache-Control no-store, returns pages[{pageId:'0', url, pageUrl:'', startTimeMs, endTimeMs}] (the desktop stream spans tabs, so there is no per-page URL); the page route returns the playlist with Content-Type application/vnd.apple.mpegurl; recordings are refused under ZDR and use a dedicated BrowserReplay rate-limit mode.
verevonRelevance: Quarry has a timeline and receipts but no video-style recording (baseline section 8); recording must be ZDR-gated exactly like this if added.
notes: The replay API shape (pages[]) anticipates per-tab recordings but currently returns one.

name: Prompt-driven interact loop: AX-tree snapshots with element refs and a one-tool agent
what: Natural-language interact runs a model that drives the browser through an accessibility-tree CLI (agent-browser): it gets an initial interactive snapshot with @e refs, issues click, fill, type, press, select, scroll, wait, find, frame, eval and get commands, re-snapshots after page changes, and returns a human-readable answer.
how: executePromptViaBrowserAgent uses the Vercel AI SDK generateText with a single 'browser' tool that runs bash commands inside the Hangar browser; MAX_STEPS 25; snapshots capped at 40 000 chars; each step prepends an ACTION LOG with common-mistake reminders (stale refs, forgot Enter); opening new tabs or URLs is blocked by regex; the agent starts on the scrape's page; model gemini-3.5-flash via Vertex (GenAI fallback), zero-data-retention uses an OpenAI model with store:false; LangSmith tracing is bypassed for ZDR.
verevonRelevance: Contradicts the scout's negative finding: Firecrawl does use AX snapshots with refs. Verevon forbids an in-process loop in Quarry (Model plans, Quarry executes), but the one-command-per-step tool contract, ref invalidation rule and action-log reflection are directly reusable in the Model Plane's loop calling Quarry /step.
notes: Quality 4: pragmatic and bounded; weaknesses are a regex-only tab guard, no per-step approvals and a free-form bash tool (broad capability).

name: Code execution inside a live session (node, python, bash)
what: Callers can run their own code against a live browser: node code runs with Playwright page and context objects in scope, python and bash run alongside; output returns stdout, stderr, result, exitCode, killed and truncated.
how: browserExecuteRequestSchema (language node default, timeout 1-300 s, code <=100 000 bytes) is forwarded to Hangar execute; the interact controller reuses it for the code branch; Safe Mode rejects the whole feature; rate limit BrowserExecute is the most generous browser mode.
verevonRelevance: Quarry allows evaluate and raw-CSS actions without approval (baseline Known gap 12); arbitrary code execution is the extreme version of that, so Verevon should expose it only behind Model Plane approval classes and sandbox rules.
notes: Powerful and risky by design; Firecrawl contains it by tenant isolation and bans it for Safe Mode orgs.

name: Prompt-injection guard as a scrape option (checkPromptInjection)
what: checkPromptInjection:true scans page markdown with a classifier before any LLM-backed format runs and blocks the scrape with 403 SCRAPE_PROMPT_INJECTION_DETECTED when the content tries to steer an AI; the fee is charged only if every chunk got a verdict.
how: performPromptInjectionGuard runs first in the transformer chain; checkForPromptInjection chunks content (32 000 chars, 2 000 overlap, concurrency 5) and asks gpt-4o-mini for {isInjection, reason}; the system prompt randomises the delimiter tag so page text cannot spoof it and defines injection by capability (requests an agent could act on) while treating llms.txt-style agent onboarding notes and human-directed CTAs as benign; failing chunks fail open and are unbilled; a deprecated copy on the json format is lifted to the top-level flag.
verevonRelevance: Baseline Known gap 12: Quarry has no prompt-injection defences; an opt-in, billed, fail-open scan at the ingestion edge (with Model Plane as classifier host) plus observation labelling would close the largest agent-safety hole.
notes: Fail-open is a deliberate trade-off; Verevon may prefer fail-closed for agent-bound content.

name: Human approval and terms gates for paid agent tool calls
what: An agent run can be told to ask before spending: exchange.requireApproval with maxCalls (1-30) pauses at a pendingApproval listing each call (provider, capability, input, estimated credits); the caller approves specific callIds (optionally 'always') or declines; provider data terms are never auto-accepted by the agent.
how: agentExchangeSchema {enabled, toolkits, maxCalls, requireApproval, approve{approvalId, callIds, always}, decline{approvalId}, onTermsRequired skip|ask}; status returns pendingApproval of kind calls or terms and an exchange summary (paidCalls, creditsUsed, skippedProviders, requiresAction accept_terms with terms/show and terms/accept capability payloads and confirmed:true); a comment states only a human-authorised terms/accept or the dashboard may accept terms.
verevonRelevance: Maps onto Verevon's approval model (approvals live in Model Plane/Application, not Quarry): the approvalId + callIds + 'always' shape and the rule 'terms acceptance is never automatic' are reusable for connector and paid-provider actions.

name: Domain scoping for agent runs
what: Agent runs can be constrained to the supplied URLs (strictConstrainToURLs), given a one-off allow-list override (overrideWhitelist), and checked against threat-protection policy for start URLs, with the explicit caveat that in-page navigation in the remote browser cannot be intercepted by the API.
how: agentController checks urls with checkUrlsAgainstThreatPolicy before handing off (billing scan fees for rejected requests), emits rejected-activity SIEM events, and documents in a comment that agent-interop scrapes are enforced by the scrape pipeline while remote-browser navigation is not.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's BrowserBroker grants replace client-supplied allowed_domains with grant domains (baseline section 'constraints'), which is stricter than Firecrawl's best-effort scoping; keep that server-side authority.
notes: The caveat about unenforceable in-page navigation is a candid statement of the remote-browser limit.

name: Alexandria: provider tools discovered by search and executed through scrape
what: Search with sources:['web','alexandria'] or domainTools:true returns data.tools (provider, capability, description, matchedBy semantic|domain, matchedUrls) for free; executing a tool is a /v2/scrape call carrying alexandria:[{provider, capability, options}] (up to 10 calls, up to 120 s), and 'firecrawl/find-tools' is itself a capability.
how: scrapeController diverts bodies with an alexandria key to providerScrapeController; discoverTools queries the Exchange (limit 24, 10 s) and is refused under ZDR; SDK scrapeAlexandria generates a UUID requestId sent as x-request-id; response data.alexandria[] with per-call data or error plus data.creditsCost; tool detail levels compact|summary|full via toolDetail.
verevonRelevance: Closest analogue to integration-corev2 provider actions with discovery: 'search discovers tools, a single execution endpoint runs them' lets the Model Plane find a capability by domain or intent without a hard-coded tool list.
notes: integration-corev2 has about 142 named operations in one Execute switch (baseline section 10); a discoverable capability catalog (provider, capability, schema, price) would be the missing layer.

name: Paid provider execution with credit lock, settle and replay-safe idempotency
what: Paid provider calls follow authorize, quote, reserve (credit lock), execute, finalize, ledger write and usage report; the charge id is sha256(team, x-request-id) with a seven-day record so completed requests replay without re-execution; a different payload under the same id is 409 duplicate_request, a running one 409 request_in_flight, an uncertain outcome 503 request_unresolved.
how: services/alexandria/retrieve.ts per the README: authorize through the Exchange against organizationDataSourceAccess flags, refuse free-plan teams for paidPlanOnlyCapabilities (fail closed with 503 plan_verification_unavailable), Autumn lockCredits/finalizeCreditsLock, billing-queue job alexandria-bill-<chargeId>, forward the caller's Authorization to Exchange on execution only (never stored); mixed batches rejected before billing; settlement covered by mocked tests only.
verevonRelevance: Exactly the guarantees integration-corev2 write actions need (signed attestations exist, idempotency semantics are not documented in the baseline); copy the outcome taxonomy (completed, refused-before-execution, uncertain) and the 'uncertain stays pending for manual reconciliation' rule.
notes: README states paid settlement has not run against an Autumn sandbox, so treat it as design, not proven.

name: OAuth bearer tokens introspected with audience binding for hosted MCP
what: Besides fc- API keys, the API accepts OAuth access tokens issued for the hosted MCP server: each token is introspected, must be active, unexpired, bound to the expected resource (audience https://api.firecrawl.dev/ or the MCP audience) and carry a recognised credential purpose; inactive results are cached for 60 s and an introspection outage raises a distinct OAuthIntrospectionUnavailableError so it can be told apart from a bad token.
how: oauth-token-introspection.ts (OAUTH_INTROSPECT_URL/SECRET) returns {active, api_key, scope, client_id, team_id, exp, aud, credential_purpose general|hosted_mcp_oauth}; the token hash (sha256 prefix) is the cache key; OAuthIntrospectionUnavailableError keeps a cache outage from becoming an auth outage; WWW-Authenticate advertises protected-resource metadata so agents can discover the authorization server.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon exposes Quarry or provider actions to external MCP clients, it needs audience-bound OAuth tokens introspected by Control Plane auth-core; integration-corev2 currently exposes no MCP/tool surface (baseline section 10).
notes: Resource-indicator checks prevent a token minted for one resource being replayed at another.

name: Delegated MCP credential: short-lived HMAC token wrapping an API key
what: The hosted MCP service can present a signed fcmcp_ credential instead of a raw key; the API verifies a strict payload (v, aud firecrawl-core, purpose hosted_mcp_oauth, api_key, iat, exp), canonical base64url encoding, clock-skew limits (30 s iat, 120 s exp) and constant-time signature comparison.
how: verifyMcpDelegatedCredential(token, secret, now) with PREFIX fcmcp_, MAX_TOKEN_LENGTH 2048, exact key-set check and api_key format validation (fc- plus 32 hex, valid UUID).
verevonRelevance: A compact pattern for gateway-to-Quarry delegation without forwarding user tokens: short-lived, audience-bound, purpose-tagged; Verevon's cross-plane service tokens already follow a manifest, this adds explicit purpose and skew rules.

name: MCP action logs: team-visible audit of tool calls without leaking intent
what: The hosted MCP server writes one log row per tool call (tool name, client name/version, auth type api-key or oauth, OAuth client id, status, error class, resource, request id) to an internal ingest endpoint; teams can list their own logs through the API; the model's stated objective and API job id are stored but excluded from the team-readable columns, and ZDR teams get an accepted-but-not-stored response.
how: POST /v2/mcp/action-logs (shared-secret bearer with constant-time check, 64 KB body limit, in-process rate limit 600 per minute, actor validation against api_keys or user_teams) and GET /v2/mcp/action-logs (cursor pagination, retention window) backed by ClickHouse; ZDR returns 202 disposition zero-data-retention.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon adds an MCP front for Quarry, per-call action logs with a privacy-minimised team view are the audit contract to meet, with ZDR short-circuiting storage.
notes: Query shows objective and api_job_id are deliberately not in the team-readable column list (git #5092).

name: Slack app: OAuth install, slash commands and events
what: Teams can connect a Slack workspace (OAuth start, callback, status, channel list, disconnect) and use /monitor and /firecrawl slash commands and Slack events; monitor alerts can post to a chosen channel.
how: routes under /v2/slack with authMiddleware for start/status/channels/delete and signature verification for commands and events; Slack's 3-second ack deadline is met by acknowledging then handling asynchronously; bot tokens are encrypted at rest (SLACK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY) in slack_installations; the monitor stores only the channel id.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Application Plane owns notifications; a Slack channel destination for Quarry change alerts would route through notification-core rather than Quarry holding tokens (integration-corev2 already has a Slack connector).
notes: Do not copy token storage into Quarry; use integration-corev2's vault.

name: Monitor notification channels with double opt-in email
what: Monitor alerts can go to a webhook, Slack, or up to 25 email recipients; recipients added by a monitor owner are pending until they confirm, each has an unsubscribe token, and both confirm and unsubscribe are public endpoints authenticated only by the token.
how: monitor_email_recipients table (status pending|confirmed|unsubscribed, source team|opt_in|legacy, 256-bit base64url tokens, confirmation_sent_at, last_notified_at); POST /v2/monitor/email/confirm and /unsubscribe registered before /monitor/:id; in-app notifications and Resend email are separate services; includeDiffs controls whether diffs are embedded.
verevonRelevance: Quarry change webhooks fan out to notification-core (baseline section 1); the pending/confirmed/unsubscribed recipient model is the compliance detail to add if user-supplied external recipients are ever allowed.

name: Partner admin provisioning API
what: A path-secret-gated admin surface lets an integration partner create users, validate API keys and rotate keys, proxied to an integrations service; requests are tagged by integration.
how: routes/admin.ts under /admin/<BULL_AUTH_KEY>/ (secret in the path) plus POST /admin/integration/create-user, /validate-api-key, /rotate-api-key via lib/admin-integration-integrations-proxy with an S2S secret.
verevonRelevance: A secret-in-URL admin gate is not an acceptable pattern for Verevon (use Control Plane principals); only the capability list (create, validate, rotate) is informative for partner onboarding.
notes: Weakness: the BULL_AUTH_KEY path secret protects admin metrics and the queue UI.

name: Scrape-to-index sinks: shared page index and a sampled search-index feed
what: Successful scrapes are written, via a RabbitMQ indexer queue, to an index of cached documents (object in storage plus an index database row) that later serves maxAge cache hits and map discovery; a separate sampled feed (default 10 percent) sends documents to a search service for the search/highlights products.
how: transformers/index.ts samples by traffic share when INDEXER_RABBITMQ_URL is set and publishes through services/indexing/indexer-queue (amqplib); sendDocumentToSearchIndex checks ENABLE_SEARCH_INDEX and SEARCH_SERVICE_URL, applies SEARCH_INDEX_SAMPLE_RATE, skips empty or unsuitable documents and passes the GCS path {indexId}.json; the index lives in a separate database (db/schema/index-db.ts) keyed by URL hash with per-domain maxAge metadata.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's equivalent is Quarry ingest into the Data Plane (documents plus source trace); the Firecrawl difference is an implicit cross-tenant shared cache, which Verevon must not copy because of ZDR and owner-plane ACL rules.
notes: Cross-tenant shared index is a privacy decision specific to the hosted product (ZDR requests skip it). Corrects the scout, which described a single RabbitMQ index worker.

name: Zero-data-retention support is uneven across endpoints and explicitly refused where unsafe
what: ZDR is honoured on scrape, search, crawl, batch, browser/interact and parse, but explicitly refused or degraded elsewhere: agent and extract (400), monitors (400, needs retained snapshots), change tracking and onlyCleanContent (warning, feature skipped), scrape-status retrieval (400), provider tools/Alexandria (403), recordings and profiles (400), MCP action logs (accepted, not stored).
how: Per-request zeroDataRetention plus team flag modes (scrape and search disabled|allowed|forced); ZDR requests suppress OpenTelemetry tracing and the flag is carried through worker job logging and indexing helpers (the retention behaviour of each sink was not traced); the zdrCost surcharge applies; each unsupported combination returns an explicit error or warning rather than silently retaining data.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's rule 'ZDR must propagate through any content-persisting boundary' needs exactly this per-feature refusal matrix: Quarry already refuses durable crawl/batch under ZDR and returns no text on ZDR scrapes (baseline section 2), so adopt explicit 'unsupported under ZDR' errors instead of empty outputs.
notes: Contrast: a Quarry ZDR scrape returns no page text at all because artifacts are not written; Firecrawl returns the document in the response and persists nothing.

name: Features Firecrawl retired: v1 deep research and llms.txt generation
what: v1 deep-research is deprecated in favour of search, and v1 llms.txt generation is deprecated with no replacement; both remain mounted for old clients and the JS SDK marks them deprecated.
how: deprecations registry entries v1_deep_research, v1_deep_research_status ('Use /v2/search instead') and v1_llmstxt ('will not be replaced'); lib/deep-research and lib/generate-llmstxt are kept only behind deprecated routes.
verevonRelevance: Quarry GAP.md plans a /v1/deep-research (Post-V2) and Features.md claims a research workflow that does not exist (baseline discrepancy 1); Firecrawl's retreat suggests investing in search plus agent threads rather than a bespoke deep-research endpoint.
notes: GAP.md section 6 marks /v1/deep-research as present in Firecrawl; it is deprecated there.

name: Docs written for agents: per-language source-of-truth pages
what: Skills instruct coding agents to read language-specific 'agent-source-of-truth' pages (Node, Python, Rust, Java, Elixir, cURL) for exact request schemas, while the skills themselves only say when and why to use each endpoint.
how: skills/firecrawl-build/SKILL.md lists docs.firecrawl.dev/agent-source-of-truth/<lang> as canonical; build skills deliberately avoid duplicating parameter docs; a verification reference requires a smoke test that proves a real request succeeds.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon's Quarry tool descriptions and SDK docs: keep routing guidance (when to use which endpoint) separate from machine-generated parameter docs, and make a smoke-test step part of any agent-facing skill.
notes: The pages are external and were not fetched.

name: Workflow skills for repeatable deliverables (external repo)
what: A separate firecrawl-workflows repository packages repeatable, Firecrawl-powered deliverables such as competitor analysis and website design-clone briefs as workflow skills.
how: Only a README pointer exists in this repo; skills/README.md routes workflow skills to firecrawl/firecrawl-workflows and mirrors the catalog.
verevonRelevance: Higher-level, outcome-shaped skills on top of the acquisition API (competitor brief, design clone using the branding format) are the product layer Verevon could ship as Space or Application Plane workflows.
notes: Content of the workflows was not available in the repo.

name: Playwright microservice: the minimal self-hosted browser engine API
what: The open-source stack renders JS pages through a small Express service: POST /scrape {url, wait_after_load, timeout (15 s default), headers, check_selector, skip_tls_verification} returns content, final URL, status and headers; GET /health reports active pages.
how: apps/playwright-service-ts uses Playwright with a page semaphore (MAX_CONCURRENT_PAGES), optional media blocking (BLOCK_MEDIA), service workers blocked, user-agent randomisation, proxy-chain for authenticated upstream proxies and an SSRF check (isInternalHost); there is no screenshot or PDF endpoint, so self-hosted users lack actions and screenshots (cloud-only fire-engine).
verevonRelevance: Shows the gap between the OSS browser engine and the hosted one; Quarry's local chromiumoxide with CDP DevTools collectors and per-session egress proxy is already far ahead of this service.
notes: Quality 2 reflects the self-host engine only.

name: Learned per-domain engine choice (engine picker)
what: A background job compares a domain's output from the cheap TLS-client engine against a real browser (LLM judges equivalence, Rust computes a verdict) and records TlsClientOk, ChromeCdpRequired or Uncertain so later scrapes of that domain can prefer the cheaper engine.
how: lib/engpicker.ts evaluates URLs with forceEngine, maxAge 0 and storeInCache false through scrapeURL, asks gpt-4o-mini for success via generateObject, and computeEngpickerVerdict (native) returns the verdict persisted in engpicker_verdicts; the waterfall prioritises tlsclient when the verdict says so and the request opts in through __experimental_engpicker.
verevonRelevance: Quarry's FallbackDriver escalates per request on block signals; persisting a per-domain 'needs browser' verdict (the sovereign reliability layer's domain intelligence registry) would cut browser cost while keeping the fast path fast.
notes: Experimental opt-in; efficacy unproven in this repo.
